title: Beef Bourguignon
ingredients: 2 pounds beef chuck, cut into 2-inch cubes
method: Combine wine, sliced onions, carrots, brandy, garlic, peppercorns, salt, parsley, and bay leaf in a large bowl. Add beef, coat well, cover, and refrigerate for 24–48 hours.
Preheat oven to 300°F (150°C).
Strain beef and vegetables from marinade; reserve liquid. Pat beef dry.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a skillet and brown beef in batches. Transfer to a bowl.
Cook bacon in the same skillet until lightly browned; transfer to beef.
Deglaze skillet with 1 cup marinade, scraping browned bits; return liquid to reserved marinade.
Heat remaining oil and sauté chopped onions for 2–3 minutes. Add strained vegetables and cook briefly. Transfer to beef.
Stir flour into skillet drippings and cook 1–2 minutes. Add garlic and tomato paste.
Add broth, remaining marinade, salt, and pepper. Bring to a boil, whisking to remove lumps.
Pour liquid over beef and vegetables in a Dutch oven. Cover and bake for 3 hours, stirring occasionally.
Sauté mushrooms in butter until browned; stir into stew before serving.

title: Ratatouille
method: Heat olive oil in a large pot and sauté onions and garlic until softened.
Add eggplant and cook for 5 minutes.
Add zucchini and bell peppers; cook until slightly tender.
Stir in tomatoes, thyme, salt, and pepper.
Reduce heat and simmer for 30–40 minutes until vegetables are soft and flavors meld.

title: French Onion Soup
method: Melt butter with olive oil in a pot. Add onions and sugar; cook on low heat for 30–40 minutes until caramelized.
Add wine and reduce by half.
Add broth, thyme, salt, and pepper. Simmer for 20 minutes.
Toast baguette slices and top with Gruyère.
Ladle soup into bowls, top with cheese toasts, and broil until melted.

title: Quiche Lorraine
method: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Blind-bake pie crust for 10 minutes.
Cook bacon until crisp; drain.
Whisk eggs, cream, nutmeg, salt, and pepper.
Spread bacon and cheese in crust; pour custard over.
Bake 30–35 minutes until set.

title: Bouillabaisse
method: Heat olive oil and sauté onion, fennel, and garlic until softened.
Add tomatoes and saffron; cook 5 minutes.
Pour in fish stock and simmer 15 minutes.
Add fish, mussels, and shrimp; cook until seafood is done.
Season and serve with crusty bread.

title: Crêpes
method: Whisk flour, sugar, and salt. Add eggs and milk gradually.
Whisk until smooth; rest batter 30 minutes.
Heat a lightly oiled pan and cook thin crêpes 1 minute per side.

title: Cassoulet
method: Soak beans overnight and cook until tender.
Brown sausage and pork belly.
Combine beans, meats, tomatoes, garlic, and thyme in a casserole.
Bake at 300°F (150°C) for 2–3 hours until thick.

title: Tartiflette
method: Boil potatoes until tender.
Cook bacon and onions until soft.
Layer potatoes, bacon mixture, and cheese in a baking dish.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 30–40 minutes.

title: Madeleines
method: Whisk eggs and sugar until pale.
Fold in flour, baking powder, zest, and butter.
Chill batter 1 hour.
Bake in madeleine molds at 375°F (190°C) for 10–12 minutes.

title: Clafoutis
method: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Arrange cherries in a buttered dish.
Whisk eggs, milk, sugar, flour, and vanilla.
Pour over cherries and bake 35 minutes.

title: Croque Monsieur
method: Spread béchamel on bread slices.
Add ham and cheese; top with another slice.
Butter outside and grill until golden.

title: Soupe au Pistou
method: Cook white beans until tender.
Add potatoes, tomatoes, and pasta; simmer until cooked.
Blend basil, garlic, and olive oil into pistou.
Stir pistou into soup before serving.

title: Gratin Dauphinois
method: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Layer potatoes with cream, garlic, nutmeg, salt, and pepper.
Dot with butter and bake 60 minutes.

title: Salade Niçoise
method: Arrange potatoes, beans, eggs, tomatoes, olives, and tuna on a plate.
Whisk oil, vinegar, and mustard.
Drizzle dressing over salad.

title: Crème Brûlée
method: Preheat oven to 325°F (160°C).
Heat cream with vanilla until warm.
Whisk yolks and sugar; slowly add warm cream.
Pour into ramekins and bake in a water bath for 35–40 minutes.
Chill, then torch sugar on top to caramelize.
